messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated DNS failures and >30% 5xx from private connectors in azure-brazilsouth to on-prem customers. Auto-pager sent to #incidents and oncall.

Priya (oncall-net): seeing the same. Private Dedicated clusters in BR South reporting slow name resolution + intermittent connection resets to onprem. Customers on Direct-Connect/ExpressRoute-equivalent reported degraded traffic.

Marco (sre): heard customers getting TLS handshakes timing out? can you paste a quick `dig` and `traceroute` from one affected host?

Priya (oncall-net): yep. from a dedicated infra node:
```
$ dig +short api.private.redwood.example.svc.azure-brazilsouth
# returns empty intermittently
$ dig api.private.redwood.example.svc.azure-brazilsouth A
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
traceroute shows path drops around `be-r01-azgw` hop.

Jae (eng-infra): running `az network watcher packet-capture` on the gateway now and collecting pcap. kicking off BGP debug snapshot with our partner. ping to upstream DNS (10.11.254.2) sometimes replies with RST.

Marco (sre): ok at least DNS is failing. Could be control-plane issue returning stale split-horizon answers for private zones. Anyone see recent config pushes in Brazilsouth private DNS? @Jae

Jae (eng-infra): no config pushes from our side in the last 24h. Azure control plane shows partial redeploy logs around 2026-04-08T03:xxZ in their status page (linked: https://status.azure.com/servicestatus). Opening ticket with Azure networking -> referencing case 987654321.

Priya (oncall-net): mitigation idea: failover affected customers to dedicated egress in westus temporarily (policy-based routing) while we work with Azure. Can we announce outage window to customers and apply route override? @Olivia can you draft notice?

Olivia (customer-success): on it. short message: "We’re observing intermittent connectivity for Private deployments in Azure Brazilsouth affecting outbound connections. Engineers are investigating. We have a temporary failover option available and will reach out to impacted customers with details." Will DM impacted list once Marco/Jae confirm.

Marco (sre): quick mitigation steps:
1) Add temporary NAT egress for affected tenant VNETs pointing to westus egress appliance (policy route). (low risk)
2) Enable DNS-proxy fallback: configure resolver chain to prefer global public-forwarder when private resolution fails (TTL short). (medium risk)
3) If control plane returns bad answers, we can flush local cache and pin to manual records via /etc/hosts for control-plane-only routes (manual, short-lived).

Jae (eng-infra): implementing #1 now for the highest-impact customers. running terraform patch to create route table and next-hop. will rollback automatically when Azure confirms control-plane stabilize.

Priya (oncall-net): logging what I see in router logs – multiple TCP resets from 10.11.254.2 -> ephemeral ports. This looks like a DNS server instance flapping behind the LB.

NetworkOpsBot: automated note: BGP session to azure-peering-02 reported 3 route flaps in 10m. See telemetry id 0x5d3a.

Marco (sre): good to know. next: prioritize customers with active onprem egress circuits. Olivia, please collect the top 8 impacted tenants and tag them with severity. I'll open an internal RCA tracking doc when we stabilize.

Olivia (customer-success): list sent to #cs and DM'ing affected contacts. adding "safe fallback" instructions for customers that can re-point to public endpoints.

Priya (oncall-net): progress update: first two customers switched to westus egress, measured reduced 5xx and DNS resolves normal there. still intermittent for the rest.

Jae (eng-infra): Packet capture uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident/2461209876/pcap.gz. Azure case 987654321 updated with capture and logs. Requested expedited call with Azure NOC.

Marco (sre): escalation plan: if Azure NOC can't provide recovery in 60m, we do a broader region-level failover plan (traffic re-route + temporary config to prefer westus or southeastasia depending on proximity). Notify legal/compliance for any egress region change.

Priya (oncall-net): adding runbook snippets used:
```
# terraform snippet (route override)
resource "azurerm_route_table" "tmp_failover" {
  name = "rt-failover-2461209876"
  resource_group_name = var.rg
}
# attach and add route 0.0.0.0/0 -> westus-egress-ip
```

Marco (sre): handoff plan: I'm taking ownership for the next 45m while Priya focuses on packet capture analysis. After that Jae will be 2nd oncall if the Azure NOC call hasn't resolved.

Priya (oncall-net): ack. leaving notes: captured these DNS answers that look wrong:
```
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.private....  300 IN A 10.200.200.200  # internal address not present in our IPAM
```
Which indicates control plane leak of internal records.

NetworkOpsBot: automated note: customer-facing SLA impacted: 3 tenants currently flagged. Incident severity raised to Sev2.

Olivia (customer-success): drafting more detailed customer outreach now that we have mitigation steps. will include rollback steps and ETA.

Jae (eng-infra): Azure NOC call scheduled in 12m. joining.

Marco (sre): summary update for the thread so far: root cause suspected: Azure control-plane DNS allocation instability in brazilsouth causing leaked/stale private answers + associated gateway flaps. Mitigation in flight: temporary egress routing to westus for critical tenants, DNS fallback chain, contacting Azure NOC. Impact: Private/on-prem-connected workloads in brazilsouth with expressroute-like circuits experiencing timeouts and 5xx.

Priya (oncall-net): FYI leaving a note for postmortem: include packet captures, Azure NOC timeline, affected tenants, mitigation timings, and any infra code changes (route table apply/rollback).

Marco (sre): tagging for follow-up: @Jae please keep collecting pcap + Azure debug, @Olivia keep CS comms, I'll maintain incident doc and timeline. If anyone needs to join the bridge DM me. :phone:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Azure reports partial control-plane degradation in brazilsouth for Private DNS and Gateway services. NOC ticket 987654321. Will update threads when change occurs.
